entries.clue: Hotel manager upset a choirmaster (6,6)

indicators.note: the letters are knocked over and rearranged

annotation.surface: A hotel manager has somehow offended the choirmaster booked to stay.
annotation.walkthrough: Gareth Malone is a British TV choirmaster, known for forming choirs from scratch in shows like The Choir; the whole of 'Hotel manager' is the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Malone is one particular choirmaster, known for building choirs from scratch on television.

entries.clue: Fungal-like internal growth (4)

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the letters of the words before it

annotation.surface: A botanist describes a lump that looks like a fungus growing inside something.
annotation.walkthrough: The hyphen hides the join: GAL ends 'Fungal' and the second L starts 'like'. 'Fungal-like' reads as a description of the growth, which is exactly why it is easy to miss as the source.
annotation.definitionFit: A gall is an abnormal swelling on a plant, a growth caused by insects, fungi or mites.

entries.clue: Right way out is to go back (7)

annotation.surface: Advice that the correct exit is the way you came in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Right way out' reads as one phrase about the proper exit; split it into Right and 'way out', a formal word for an exit.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: regress, from Latin for stepping back, is used of patients or pupils slipping back to an earlier state.

entries.clue: Silent attic is disturbed (5)

indicators.note: the letters of 'attic' are moved out of place

annotation.surface: A quiet attic has had its peace broken, perhaps by something upstairs.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pits 'Silent' against 'disturbed' as opposites in one room, which hides that 'Silent' is the definition and the attic supplies the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Tacit means unspoken, understood without being said: silent.

entries.clue: Poor man with mug wants this much champagne (6)

indicators.note: the letters are in poor shape, so rearranged

annotation.surface: A penniless man holding a mug hopes it will be filled with champagne.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Poor man' reads as a pauper, but 'Poor' works on the letters of man and mug together. The definition names a quantity: a magnum is a double-size bottle.
annotation.definitionFit: A magnum is a 1.5-litre bottle, a measure of champagne.

entries.clue: Yearn before an attempt in the distant past (4,3)

indicators.note: LONG comes before the rest in the answer

annotation.surface: Someone pines for a chance they had in the distant past.
annotation.walkthrough: Every word is used in its ordinary sense, just read as three separate pieces; 'before' only fixes the order.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for an adverbial phrase: 'it happened long ago' and 'it happened in the distant past' swap cleanly.

entries.clue: English entertained by pleasant relative (5)

indicators.note: the host takes the guest inside it

annotation.surface: An English visitor is hosted by a friendly relative.
annotation.walkthrough: 'entertained by' reads as hospitality, a guest welcomed by a kind relative; in crosswords a host that entertains a word holds it inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: a sibling's daughter is one kind of family member.

entries.clue: Russian empress confused artisan (7)

indicators.note: the letters of 'artisan' are mixed up

annotation.surface: A craftsman is bewildered in the presence of a Russian empress.
annotation.walkthrough: 'confused' sits beside 'artisan' as if describing him; it is the instruction to shuffle his letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A tsarina was the wife of a tsar, or an empress ruling Russia.

entries.clue: Reason to have record, I see (5)

annotation.surface: Someone explains why they keep a record: so they can see what happened.
annotation.walkthrough: 'I see' reads as a nod of understanding; here it supplies two pieces, the I and a C for its name.
annotation.definitionFit: Logic is reasoning, as in 'the logic behind it'.

entries.clue: Woman is in to receive southern seabirds (7)

indicators.note: 'is in' says the woman is inside something, as a person is in a house, so her letters go inside another word

blocks.note: to get = to receive; the container
a woman's name; goes inside after the G
S = southern, added at the end

annotation.surface: A woman is at home, waiting to take delivery of something from the south.
annotation.walkthrough: 'is in' reads as the woman being at home, and 'to receive' as her reason; really 'to receive' is the word the woman is put inside.
annotation.definitionFit: Gannets are large seabirds that dive for fish.

entries.clue: Owner of many tables fixed suture at rear (12)

indicators.note: the letters are repaired into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone who owns a lot of furniture had stitches put in their backside.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Owner of many tables' sounds like a furniture collector; the tables are in a restaurant. 'fixed suture' reads as a medical repair.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: someone who runs an eating place has a room full of tables to fill each night.

entries.clue: Get side transformed – most experimental! (7)

indicators.note: the letters are changed into a new form

annotation.surface: A manager urges a team to reinvent itself and be as daring as possible.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Get side' reads as a command about a team; both words are just letters, with 'transformed' telling you to rework them.
annotation.definitionFit: Edgy art or fashion is avant-garde, so the edgiest is the most experimental.

entries.clue: Misdeal distributed with no energy, dreary (6)

indicators.note: the cards, and so the letters, are dealt out in a new order
'with no' means lacking, so the word that follows is left out of the fodder

annotation.surface: A card game goes wrong, the hands dealt out listlessly, and the evening is dull.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Misdeal distributed' fits a card table perfectly, which hides that 'distributed' shuffles the letters once the E is gone.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a dismal day and a dreary day are equally grey and depressing.

entries.clue: A den Rod artfully decorated (7)

indicators.note: the letters are arranged with artistry into a new order

annotation.surface: A man called Rod has done up his den with some flair.
annotation.walkthrough: 'artfully' reads as praise for Rod's decorating; it is the instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the past tense: a room adorned with garlands has been decorated with them.

entries.clue: One bird or two, it's said, are able (6)

indicators.note: tells you to go by how 'two' is spoken

blocks.note: the number two, spelt as a different word that sounds the same

annotation.surface: A riddle about whether one bird or a pair of them can manage something.
annotation.walkthrough: The joke is the old slogan line 'two can': say TOUCAN and you hear 'two can'. 'One bird or two' sets up a count that is not a count.
annotation.definitionFit: A toucan is a single bird, the big-billed tropical one.

entries.clue: Reflector in case, yet broken (4-3)

indicators.note: the letters are broken up and reassembled

annotation.surface: A reflector is still in its packaging and yet it has been broken.
annotation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like part of the fodder but only joins; CASE YET alone has the seven letters. Cat's-eyes are the reflective studs set into British road markings.
annotation.definitionFit: A cat's-eye is a road reflector that shines in headlights.

entries.clue: Following energy loss, I get Indian vegetable (6)

indicators.note: the E is lost from BEHIND

blocks.note: as printed, added at the end

annotation.surface: Someone recovering from exhaustion is prescribed an Indian vegetable.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Following' reads as 'after'; here it is the word BEHIND, which loses its E.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional name: the green pods called okra or ladies' fingers elsewhere go by this name in Hindi and on curry-house menus.

entries.clue: Well old, caught with headlight on again (2,4,6)

indicators.note: the letters are made over again, in a new order

annotation.surface: An old driver is caught out with the headlight left on once more.
annotation.walkthrough: 'caught' looks like the usual C, but no C is in the answer: it only joins O to the rest.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the adjective, not the noun: 'she is well' and 'she is in good health' say the same.

entries.clue: Thousand wander to trees (5)

annotation.surface: A thousand people drift off into the woods.
annotation.walkthrough: G for a thousand comes from 'grand', slang for a thousand pounds or dollars.
annotation.definitionFit: A collective word standing for its members: an orchard or copse of trees is named by the one word.

entries.clue: Monk and sailor with black books (5)

blocks.note: OT = Old Testament, a set of books

annotation.surface: A monk and a sailor carry black-bound books.
annotation.walkthrough: 'books' is a common crossword shorthand for one of the two Testaments, OT or NT; the monk's presence makes the Bible reading natural.
annotation.definitionFit: An abbot is the monk who heads an abbey.

entries.clue: Piste runners kiss unexpectedly (4)

indicators.note: the letters turn up in an unexpected order

annotation.surface: Two skiers on the slope share a sudden kiss.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Piste runners' sounds like people racing downhill; the runners are the skis themselves.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: runners are the long blades a sledge slides on, and these are the ones used on a ski slope.

entries.clue: Admitted to office, small, shabby and trendy (5,2)

annotation.surface: A new official arrives looking small, scruffy and oddly fashionable.
annotation.walkthrough: The three adjectives read as a description of the new official; each is simply a piece, taken in order.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: officials take an oath on entering the job, so the oath-taking names the admission.

entries.clue: Bill about right to snap (5)

indicators.note: the bill goes around the R

blocks.note: a bird's bill is its beak; the container

annotation.surface: A man called Bill is on the point of losing his temper.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bill' reads as a name; it is a bird's beak.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym with two senses: a twig can snap or break, and so can a person's patience, the sense the surface uses.

entries.clue: Female teacher desires maths, improbably (12)

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in an unlikely way

annotation.surface: A teacher surprisingly longs for more mathematics.
annotation.walkthrough: 'improbably' reads as a comment on anyone wanting more maths; it is the signal to rearrange the two words before it.
annotation.definitionFit: A headmistress is the woman at the head of a school, a teacher.
